transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

It’s likely the hob’s overheating protection is kicking in because it can’t dissipate heat fast enough on high power. This often happens if the internal cooling fan has failed, the vents are blocked by clutter or cabinetry, or a temperature sensor is acting up. Please make sure there are no items blocking the ventilation slots around the edges and that nothing is sitting directly above the hob. Also, check if you have any child-lock or time-limit settings active that might be resetting the zones automatically.
nothing on top of it, not sure what vent slots you mean tbh. no child lock on that i know of. its only on high that it does it, low is fine

Since those checks didn't fix it, the issue is likely internal, such as a cooling fan or sensor failure. To help me find the right part for your specific model, could you please tell me the make and model number? It's usually on a label on the underside of the hob or on the guarantee card. If you can't reach that label right now, we can wait until you have it to hand.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a samsung, dont know the model and im not looking under it. a new drawer unit was fitted under it last month tho, its been doing it since then

The fact that this started after a drawer unit was fitted suggests the cabinetry might be blocking the hob's required airflow or trapping heat underneath. Please check if there are any vents on the underside of the worktop or around the hob frame that could now be obstructed by the new drawers. If those areas are clear, it’s likely an internal component like a cooling fan has failed and needs replacing. You can find the specific model number later on the guarantee card or the side edge of the hob to get the right part.
not removing the drawer or looking under it. fan roars loudly before it cuts out tho. so what now?

The loud roaring fan followed by a cut-out strongly suggests the cooling system is struggling, likely due to a failing fan bearing or a blockage in the ventilation path. Since you can't check under it right now, the next step is to ensure no new cabinetry parts are obstructing the hob's air intake or exhaust vents on the worktop surface. If those external vents are clear, the internal cooling fan assembly probably needs replacing. You can find the model number later on the side edge of the hob frame or in your user manual to order the correct part.
i said im not looking under it or removing the drawer. nothing else i can check, so do i need an engineer or what?

Yes, you will need an engineer because the loud roaring fan followed by a cut-out points to a failed internal cooling fan or a sensor issue that requires replacement. Since you cannot access the underside to check for obstructions from the new drawer unit, this is beyond safe owner repair. The hob's safety system is triggering to prevent damage, and continuing to force it on high could cause further faults. You can find the model number later on the side edge of the hob frame or in your user manual if you need to order a part for the engineer.
